annotation.authors_or_issuer: Aidonojie, P.A.; Gusite, B.; Oviosun, B.A.; Ayuba, D.; Ibrahim, N.
key_provisions_or_claims: Nigeria lacks a comprehensive AI law and national AI strategy, leaving gaps on liability, IP and ethics.
Existing laws (NDPA 2023, Cybercrimes Act 2015, Copyright Act 2022) only indirectly address AI.
Copyright Act does not recognise non-human authorship, leaving AI-generated works' ownership unclear.
AI automation threatens jobs and widens the digital divide.
Recommends robust AI regulatory framework, AI education, and stronger data privacy law.
annotation.summary_en: Doctrinal legal study of Nigeria's AI governance gaps, reviewing the Constitution, Data Protection Act 2023, Cybercrimes Act 2015 and Copyright Act 2022. It finds inconsistent regulation, weak ethics guidance, liability and IP uncertainty and job-loss risks, and calls for comprehensive AI legislation, AI education and stronger data privacy law.
annotation.title_clean: Artificial Intelligence, Law, and Society: Towards a Sustainable Governance Framework in Nigeria
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence, Law, and Society: Towards a Sustainable Governance Framework in Nigeria
